extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen-, surpass or overstep, in file order. Uses of "immanent philosophy" as the name of the Berkeley-Hume line are recorded only where the transcendent is at issue in the same place.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-971): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read. The First to Fourth and Sixth to Eighth Lectures carry none.

units.claim: The thought of pure immanence, in which all transcendence must announce and exhibit itself, remains authoritative for Locke despite his dogmatism.
units.quote: Yet the thought of pure immanence, in which all transcendence must announce and exhibit itself, remains for Locke too, despite all naive inconsequence of the dogmatistic procedure, authoritative.

units.claim: Husserl distinguishes the immanent intentional object of a consciousness, conscious as such, from the object simply, asserted as being in truth.
units.quote: we will do well to distinguish: the immanent object of the respective consciousness (the immanent intentional one), as the in the immanence of this consciousness conscious as such; and the object simply

units.claim: The immanence of the intentional object in its consciousness is not a real immanence or being-contained, and to regard it so would be countersense.
units.quote: This essentially inseparable immanence is therefore no real immanence, no real being-contained; to regard it so would be evident countersense.

units.claim: Consciousness-synthesis has, in the form of its poles, immanent contents that are irreal, unlike the real components of a real.
units.quote: A real has real components, real parts and moments, real conjunction-forms; but consciousness-synthesis has, in the form of these poles, immanent contents that are irreal (irreal).

units.claim: An inference from sense-data to a transcendent cause as a je ne sais quoi is senseless, since in the own immanent sphere every analogue of it fails.
units.quote: But senseless is an inference to a je ne sais quoi, a principially unexperienceable, for which in the own immanent sphere every analogue fails.

units.claim: The only way to transcend one's own subjectivity and self-experienced nature is empathy into another subjectivity.
units.quote: The only way to transcend the own subjectivity and self-experienced nature, Husserl states — and here intersubjectivity enters the analysis for the first time — is empathy (Einfühlung) into another subjectivity

units.claim: The inner images and signs on the tabula rasa, taken as images and signs for a transcendent nature, are inventions of a misled reflection.
units.quote: these entire inner images and signs on the tabula rasa — images and signs for a transcendent nature — are inventions of a misled reflection

units.claim: What every confirmation exhibits is the synthetic unity conscious in perception and nothing other than the outer spatial thing itself, which is from the outset the transcendent itself.
units.quote: nothing other than the outer itself, the spatial thing itself; it is from the outset the transcendent itself

units.claim: Locke's definition of cognition as perception of agreement among one's own ideas makes cognition of the principially transcendent unthinkable and so conflicts with his doctrine of transcendence.
units.quote: wherein lay that a cognition of principially transcendent is unthinkable — with which Locke's doctrine of transcendence would, to be sure, accord little

units.claim: A germ-form of the problem lies in Descartes' Meditations, whose first task is to show how the ego comes from its cogitationes to belief in a transcendent objectivity.
units.quote: insofar as their first task is to show how the ego comes, from the immediately evident domain of its cogitationes, to the belief in a transcendent objectivity, in an outer world and God

units.claim: For Berkeley association permits inference only from immanent data to immanent data, so a transcendent nature in a transcendent space is a fiction reducing to associatively unified sensation-complexes.
units.quote: infer can I so from immanent data to immanent data, never to transcendent, to unperceivable. As a transcendent nature, as a realm of transcendent material existences in a transcendent space, is a fiction

units.claim: Berkeley denies a transcending of the idea-field toward transcendent nature while admitting the transcendent in the form of foreign I's, an inference Husserl says has other foundations.
units.quote: Is it not perverse to want to deny the possibility of a transcending of the idea-field in favor of a transcendent nature, and on the other side yet to admit transcendent, namely in the form of foreign I's?

units.term: theory of transcendence on the ground of immanence
units.claim: However primitive, Berkeley's theory is the first theory of transcendence on the ground of immanence, determining the sense of the experienced world purely out of the immanently running experiences.
units.quote: it is yet a first theory of transcendence on the ground of immanence

units.claim: For Hume reason permits neither counting the appearing world as existing nor regarding it as manifestation of a further transcendent behind it.
units.quote: Reason permits here neither to let the appearing world (the imaginative thing-world substructed to the actual sensation-data) count in any sense as existing, nor permits it to regard this world as manifestation of a still-further-behind-lying transcendent.

units.claim: Hume's skepsis does not concern only the science of transcendent natural reality, since its proof is led on the immanent ground and undermines immanent psychology too.
units.quote: One may not say, Husserl insists, that the skepsis concerns only the science of the transcendent (natural) reality.

absences.expected_because: The demand for a theory of cognition is introduced here, and from the Fifteenth Lecture on the commentary frames that theory as the problem of cognizing the transcendent within immanence.
